examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Two-phase locking has a growing lock-acquisition phase and a shrinking phase after the first release; no new locks are acquired afterward. It ensures conflict serializability but can deadlock. Recoverability requires a reader to commit after the writer it depended on; avoiding dirty reads prevents cascading aborts.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
T2 reads a value written by uncommitted T1; T3 reads a value written by uncommitted T2. T1 aborts. How many other transactions require cascading rollback?

**Answer: 2.** T2 depends on a value invalidated by T1's abort and must roll back. T3 depends on T2's uncommitted output and must also roll back. Two other transactions are affected.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
Strict 2PL holds exclusive locks until commit/abort and prevents these dirty dependencies. Basic 2PL alone does not imply every strictness/recovery guarantee.

2PL can deadlock; serializability does not imply deadlock freedom.
